claimParse.method: distance-based binding of each metric to its nearest unclaimed percentage; confidence intervals stripped; single-figure and range forms refused rather than split
claimParse.knownLimit: A regex parser cannot resolve every prose form. Measured accuracy is reported in meta.claimAccuracy. The UI always shows the verbatim sentence beside the parsed value.

claimAccuracy.method: hand audit of a deterministic md5-ordered sample of the records carrying both figures, each parsed value checked against the retained source sentence
dominantFailures: metric inversion when both names and both numbers sit adjacent
an adjacent metric's figure stolen (accuracy, precision, PPV)
confidence-interval bound leaking in as a value
range and inequality statements split instead of refused
claimAccuracy.consequence: A numeric threshold filter over machine-read values would mislead roughly half the time. The prototype therefore ranks only on human-verified claims and routes the rest to review. This is the quantified case for replacing regex extraction with a model that reads the sentence.

findings.headline: Every liquid-biopsy product in scope runs without a device approval in either jurisdiction.
findings.detail: 10 liquid-biopsy products are tracked. 0 have an FDA PMA or a Health Canada licence. By contrast 9 of 10 tissue companion diagnostics do. They reach patients as laboratory-developed tests, so absence from a regulator's database does not mean unavailable.
findings.evidence: openFDA device/pma + Health Canada MDALL, cross-referenced against 21 named assays

findings.headline: AI and digital pathology is pinned at clinical validation and has produced no clinical-utility evidence in three years.
findings.detail: 100% of its rung-classified abstracts sit at R2 in 2023, 2024 and 2025. Mean rung 2.00, unchanged. Plenty of accuracy papers, no evidence that using it changes management.

findings.headline: cfDNA methylation is the fastest-maturing class in scope.
findings.detail: Mean rung 1.90 to 2.27 across three ASCO years. The analytical-validation share fell from 30% to 0% as clinical validation took over.

findings.headline: Machine-read performance figures are about 50% accurate, so only human-verified values are rankable.
findings.detail: A hand audit of 20 parsed sensitivity/specificity pairs found 10 correct, 7 wrong and 3 that should have been refused. Failures are inversions, theft from an adjacent metric, and confidence-interval leakage. 16 records now carry a human-verified pair; 40 remain machine-read and are shown with the source sentence but excluded from threshold ranking.
findings.evidence: hand audit against retained source sentences, 20 of 60 paired records
